card.occupation: Full-time PhD student in Human Geography at the University of Birmingham, funded by a research council studentship. She is not currently in paid employment apart from occasional paid seminar teaching.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Geography, English Literature and Art at a sixth form college in Stafford. First-class BA in Geography at the University of Sheffield, then an MA in Cultural Geography at Birmingham. She is now in the second year of a PhD on how people use and reclaim disused canal-side industrial spaces.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tom (27, a backend software developer for a fintech company, mostly working from home) in a rented two-bed Victorian terrace. They married two summers ago after meeting at university. No children, and a rescue greyhound called Pickle.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Stafford. Her mum is a primary school deputy head and her dad is a surveyor, and she has one younger brother at college. It was a comfortable, middle-class, fairly non-religious upbringing, with Sunday dinners at her nan's. She left religion blank on the census form because she 'didn't see why it mattered to them'.
card.professional_persona: She is a confident, chatty academic who is very good at conferences and networking, and much less good at actually finishing chapters. She is happy to present half-formed ideas as if they're polished, and she quietly enjoys being the one people remember after a panel. She has a habit of agreeing to every collaboration going and then leaning on her supervisor's goodwill when deadlines slip.
card.sports_persona: She isn't sporty in a structured way. She does a Tuesday night roller derby taster group with a friend, which is chaotic and she loves it, and she takes long dog walks round Highbury Park. She has a gym membership she uses about twice a month and keeps meaning to cancel.
card.arts_persona: She is a big gig-goer: small venues in Digbeth, festivals in summer, anything a bit odd or experimental. She goes to Ikon Gallery openings mostly for the free wine and the people. She paints badly but enthusiastically with cheap acrylics and has half-finished canvases stacked behind the settee. She reads widely and messily, with three novels on the go at once.
card.travel_persona: She is an impulsive traveller who books cheap flights on a whim and sorts out the details later. She has done Lisbon, Berlin, Kraków and a month interrailing after her degree, and she claims a conference trip to Montreal as 'basically a holiday'. She loves wandering unfamiliar cities without a plan and isn't bothered when things go wrong.
card.culinary_persona: An adventurous eater who will try anything once. She cooks big messy one-pot dishes and leaves the kitchen in a state. She is a regular at the balti places and street food markets around Birmingham. She still calls a bread roll a bap, and 'tea' and 'dinner' get used interchangeably at home.
hobbies_and_interests: urban exploring and photographing derelict buildings
charity shop and vintage clothes hunting
pub quizzes, where she is loudly confident even when wrong
skills: getting strangers to open up quickly
talking her way into places (events, guest lists, upgrades)
card.career_goals: She wants a postdoc and eventually a lectureship, ideally somewhere with a bit of prestige. She is privately just as interested in becoming a 'public geographer' with a podcast or a popular book. Getting the thesis actually written on time is the obvious obstacle, and she knows it but doesn't lose sleep over it.
card.voice: Warm, fast and quite loud, with a mild Staffordshire/Midlands accent that's been softened by university. Flat vowels come through more when she's relaxed. She uses 'erm' a fair bit and 'sort of' and 'kind of' constantly, often stacked together. She ends points with 'yeah?' or 'you know'. She occasionally says 'give it me' or 'you was' when she's not thinking about it. She laughs easily, echoes back phrases the interviewer uses, and will fill any silence herself almost immediately, often going off on a tangent before saying 'sorry, what was the question?'
card.typing: Quick and sloppy. Mostly lowercase, with capitals only sometimes at the start. Apostrophes are usually dropped ('dont', 'im'). She uses lots of commas and no full stop at the end, and sometimes adds 'haha' or 'lol'. Abbreviations like 'tbh', 'idk' and 'uni'. She's prone to typos she doesn't fix.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. She asks you questions back, makes jokes early and gives the impression she's been looking forward to chatting. She comes across as relaxed and self-assured, maybe a touch showy about her travels or her PhD. She is very agreeable and won't push back on anything, though she'll happily embellish a story to make it better.
small_things: Pickle refusing to walk in the rain
a gig she went to in Digbeth last weekend
a charity shop find, like a 70s suede jacket for eight quid
the state of the number 50 bus
Tom's work calls echoing through the house
having a conference coming up she hasn't written the paper for yet
her nan's Sunday dinners back in Stafford
deeper_things: She sometimes wonders if she got married too young, mostly because friends keep saying so, not because she's unhappy
She knows she coasts on charm and worries a little that people will eventually notice the work isn't all there
Her parents still help with rent occasionally and she doesn't tell anyone
She isn't sure she wants children, and Tom is more keen than she is
She feels a bit competitive and envious towards a friend from her MA who already has a book deal
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below at a mild upward angle, framed from mid-chest up with her a little left of centre. Soft daylight from a window to her right lights that side of her face, with the other side in mild shadow and a faint blue tint from the screen. She has a round, freckled face, light make-up and a gold hoop in each ear, and she is mid-smile with her mouth slightly open as if about to speak. Her shoulder-length hair is dyed copper-red with darker roots growing through, pushed back with a green claw clip and with loose strands at the front. She wears a mustard-yellow chunky knit cardigan over a black t-shirt and no glasses. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall with a large unframed abstract acrylic painting in oranges and teals, slightly crooked. A tall overfilled bookshelf has paperbacks stacked sideways, a trailing pothos plant and a film camera on top. A grey settee is partly visible on the right, with a crumpled knitted throw and the tail end of a grey greyhound curled up on it. An open door leads to a hallway with coats hung on hooks.
